item.title: English Station Park-Pool Donor Emerges
item.description: The Elicker administration has found a prospective financier for the park and public pool proposed to replace English Station: the Roxanne and Henry Brandt Foundation, which expressed interest on Friday in contributing up to $10 million toward the project. The post English Station Park-Pool Donor Emerges appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: $113M Overhaul Planned For State St. Station, Court St. Bridge
item.description: The state plans to invest more than $100 million in a project designed to modernize -- and attract more travelers to -- the State Street train station, prompting neighbors to push for details on a related effort to convert the adjacent Court Street bridge to pedestrian and bicycle use, only. The post $113M Overhaul Planned For State St. Station, Court St. Bridge appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: “Inappropriate” Texts Lead To Teacher’s Arrest
item.description: "I'll be up all night smoking a brisket if you need anything," a Benjamin Jepson school math teacher texted a 13-year-old former student of his at 10:50 p.m. on a Friday. After reviewing messages like that, city police have arrested the teacher on one misdemeanor count of harmful communication with a minor. The post “Inappropriate” Texts Lead To Teacher’s Arrest appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Start-Up City Campaign Launched
item.description: New Haven is starting 2026 with a civic resolution: to become a "city of yes" for small-business start-ups. That's the goal of a new campaign called "Best City to Start." The post Start-Up City Campaign Launched appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Facing Accessibility Critique, State Closes Bus Ticket Sales Outlet’s Door
item.description: All customers -- not just those in wheelchairs -- now have to wait outside to be helped at the new bus ticket sales outlet on Church Street, as the state works to make the one-step-elevated storefront "accessible for all.” The city’s disability commission, meanwhile, hosted a wide-ranging discussion about how the outlet’s accessibility problems extend beyond its lack of a ramp.
